## Overview

Your Day Master is Xin 辛 (Yin Metal), the stem of your day pillar, Xin Hai 辛亥. In BaZi the Day Master is simply the element that represents you, the point from which every other element in the chart is read. Xin is refined, precise metal — the jeweller's metal rather than the sword — and the whole reading turns on how much support it receives.

You were born in the Jia Shen 甲申 month pillar, in the season of Shen 申 (Monkey), when Metal is at its most assertive. That fits your numbers: Metal makes up 45.9% of the chart, Wood 27.1%, Water 13.5%, Fire 8.2% and Earth just 5.3%. With 51.2% of the chart in elements that support the Day Master (the Friend and Rob Wealth metal plus the Resource earth), your Day Master counts as strong. A strong Xin does not need more metal or earth; it does best when something gives it a task to work on. That is why Fire (Direct Officer, Seven Killings), Water (Hurting Officer, Eating God) and Wood (Direct and Indirect Wealth) are your favorable elements, while Earth and Metal are the unfavorable ones.

The central theme of the chart is a talented, self-contained metal nature learning to let Fire and Water move it — in plain terms, to let structure, challenge and expression shape an otherwise very independent personality. Your strongest element, Metal, gives you standards and stamina; your weakest, Earth, is scarce rather than absent, which suggests you may sometimes run short of the quiet, grounding routines that keep strong metal from becoming brittle.

## Personality

The most repeated signal in your chart is Rob Wealth, which symbolizes independence, self-reliance and a competitive streak — the impulse to do things your own way and to compare yourself with others. It appears as the Ten God of your year stem, Geng 庚 (Yang Metal), and again as the main qi hidden stem of your month branch, Shen 申 (Monkey). Sitting in the year pillar, it colours how you meet the wider world: you likely come across as capable and self-possessed, someone who would rather figure things out alone than ask. The month position, which describes your working style, reinforces it — you are quick, exacting and not easily impressed by authority.

Yet your day branch, Hai 亥 (Pig), holds Ren 壬 (Yang Water) as its main qi, a Hurting Officer: the star of sharp expression, originality and a certain resistance to being boxed in. This is the part of you that speaks plainly, questions the rules and needs creative outlet. Paired with the Friend (a peer-and-equal star) on your hour stem, Xin 辛 (Yin Metal), and the Indirect Wealth of the hour branch's main qi, Yi 乙 (Yin Wood) — the star of opportunistic, clever gain — the picture is someone with strong opinions, a dry wit and a private, resourceful inner life.

The habit worth adjusting is the Rob Wealth reflex to turn everything into a comparison. When your standards are high and your metal is strong, other people can feel measured. Letting the Hurting Officer side of you express appreciation rather than critique — and letting Fire's Direct Officer quality supply patience — softens that edge without diminishing your competence. Your Peach Blossom star, touching the hour pillar through Mao 卯 (Rabbit), suggests a natural charm that works best when it is warm rather than guarded.

## Career

Your month pillar pairs Jia 甲 (Yang Wood), a Direct Wealth stem — the star of steady, earned income and methodical work — with the Shen branch whose main qi is Rob Wealth. This combination describes a career where you want both reliability and autonomy: a role with clear deliverables but room to run your own method. The Travelling Horse symbolic star touches this same month pillar through Shen, which traditionally points to movement, travel or work that is not tied to one desk — a good fit for roles involving projects, clients or changing locations.

The Fire in your chart, though only 8.2%, is favorable, and it comes through Officer stars: Seven Killings as the main qi of your year branch, Wu 午 (Horse), and Direct Officer in the wider luck cycles. Officer stars symbolize structure, responsibility and the pressure that produces achievement. In practice this means you tend to perform best when someone or something raises the bar — a demanding brief, a visible responsibility, a deadline that matters. A completely unstructured environment may leave your strong metal restless rather than free.

Your hour pillar's Indirect Wealth (Yi 乙, main qi of Mao) adds an enterprising streak: side projects, specialist niches or unconventional routes can appeal more than a standard ladder. The strength to lean on is your precision and stamina; the habit to watch is taking on too much independently when collaboration would be faster. With Rob Wealth so prominent, delegation can feel like loss of control — but the Direct Wealth in your month stem rewards patient, shared effort more than solitary brilliance.

## Wealth

Wealth in this chart is well represented: Direct Wealth (steady salary, contracts, savings discipline) as the Ten God of your month stem, Jia 甲 (Yang Wood), and Indirect Wealth (windfalls, negotiated deals, entrepreneurial income) as the main qi of both your day branch Hai and your hour branch Mao. Having both suggests a money life with two channels — a dependable base plus something more variable on the side.

Because Wood is favorable for you (27.1% of the chart), money-making activity suits your constitution; you are not fighting your own nature when you pursue it. The caution comes from Rob Wealth, which sits in your year stem and in the main qi of your month branch. Rob Wealth symbolizes peer competition and the impulse to spend or commit alongside others; it is the star most associated with money leaking through comparison, generosity or joint ventures entered too quickly. With Metal at 45.9% and unfavorable, more metal-style accumulation for its own sake is not what balances you.

The practical shape of this is simple: keep the Direct Wealth channel disciplined and let the Indirect Wealth channel be the experimental one, kept separate in your mind. Your hour pillar's Friend stem adds another peer influence near your output, so money decisions made in company deserve an extra pause. Review your spending in the second half of each year, when annual pillars shift, rather than making changes on impulse.

## Love and Relationships

Your day branch, Hai 亥 (Pig), is the sphere of close partnership, and its main qi is Ren 壬 (Yang Water), a Hurting Officer. This star brings honesty, expressiveness and a low tolerance for pretence into intimate relationships — you want a partner who can handle directness and who has their own inner world. Its middle qi is Jia 甲 (Yang Wood), Direct Wealth, which suggests you value steadiness and practical reliability in a partner as much as chemistry.

The hour pillar, which describes later-life partnership and home life, carries Xin 辛 (Yin Metal), a Friend — the star of equality and companionship — over Mao 卯 (Rabbit), whose main qi Yi 乙 (Yin Wood) is Indirect Wealth. The Peach Blossom star touches this hour pillar through Mao, a traditional marker of attractiveness and romantic opportunity, so your charm tends to show itself in the domestic, everyday register rather than the dramatic one. A Void (Kong Wang) star, found from your day pillar, also touches the hour pillar with the branches Yin and Mao — traditionally read as a note of idealism or occasional emotional distance in that sphere, not as a lack.

The strengths here are loyalty, wit and a genuine desire for partnership between equals. The habit to adjust is the Rob Wealth streak: in conflict it can turn a conversation into a contest, and your Hurting Officer's directness can land harder than you intend. Slowing down and naming what you feel, rather than scoring a point, plays to the Fire that is favorable for you — warmth as structure, not as pressure.

## Wellbeing Habits

Your chart is metal-dominant at 45.9%, with Earth at only 5.3% — the weakest element — and Water at 13.5%. In traditional terms, strong metal with scarce earth often reads as a constitution that runs on drive and precision but can neglect rest and routine. The habits below are simply ways to build in the grounding (earth-like) and flowing (water-like) qualities your chart is thinner on; none of them is a treatment for anything.

- **Sleep:** protect a regular bedtime and a slow wind-down. Earth is your weakest element and Earth is associated with routine and centredness, so consistent hours do more for you than catching up later.
- **Food:** favour warm, cooked, unhurried meals over eating on the move. Your Rob Wealth prominence can push you to skip meals to finish a task; a steady eating rhythm suits a strong metal constitution better.
- **Movement:** mix precise, disciplined exercise (which suits your Xin metal) with something fluid — swimming, walking, stretching — to feed the Water that carries your Hurting Officer's need for expression.
- **Emotion:** give the Hurting Officer in your day branch a regular outlet — writing, music, honest conversation. Unspoken critique tends to harden in a metal-heavy chart; saying it lightly keeps it moving.

If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Current Luck Pillar

A Luck Pillar is a ten-year period, set by the traditional rules from your birth chart, whose stem and branch colour the overall tone of those years. You are in the Geng Chen 庚辰 Luck Pillar, which runs from 2022 to 2031. Its stem, Geng 庚 (Yang Metal), carries the Rob Wealth Ten God and is unfavorable; its branch, Chen 辰 (Dragon), has Direct Resource — the star of learning, support and consolidation — as the main hidden stem, and that too is unfavorable. Both halves of this decade lean on Metal and Earth, the two elements your strong Day Master least needs.

In practice, these ten years have a "more of the same, then some" rhythm: more independence, more comparison, more accumulation of knowledge and responsibility — useful raw material, but not naturally balancing. The risk is overloading yourself with commitments taken on solo, or measuring your progress against others. The opportunity is that Direct Resource is genuinely good at depth: study, credentials, patient mastery. Treat this decade as a building period rather than a performing one, and deliberately invite the favorable Fire, Water and Wood into your life — demanding projects, creative output, growth-oriented work.

The Next Luck Pillar, Ji Mao 己卯 (2032–2041), changes the balance. Its stem, Ji 己 (Yin Earth), is Indirect Resource and also unfavorable, continuing the resource-heavy theme, but its branch, Mao 卯 (Rabbit), carries Indirect Wealth as its main hidden stem and is favorable. That shift moves the emphasis from consolidation toward enterprise and negotiated gain — a decade to act on what this one has built.

## Year by Year

Each Chinese solar year begins at Li Chun, the start of spring, which falls close to the beginning of the calendar year; so the year described below runs roughly from that point to the same point the following year. All six years sit inside your Geng Chen 庚辰 Luck Pillar, and no new Luck Pillar begins in this window, so the decade's Rob Wealth and Direct Resource backdrop stays constant while the annual pillars move.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

This is a Fire year, and Fire is favorable for you. The year stem Bing 丙 (Yang Fire) is a Direct Officer — the star of structure, responsibility and legitimate authority — and the main qi of the year branch Wu 午 (Horse) is Ding 丁 (Yin Fire), a Seven Killings, the star of pressure, challenge and the drive it creates. Both are favorable, so a year that asks more of you formally — a bigger role, a visible standard, a demanding commitment — tends to bring out your best rather than drain you. Lean into structured responsibility and into the warmth and clarity Fire brings to your strong metal.

Two things deserve care. The year branch Wu forms a punishment with your year pillar branch Wu, an internal friction that can show up as restlessness or self-criticism when you push too hard; pace yourself and do not treat every setback as a verdict. The year stem Bing also combines with both your day pillar stem Xin and your hour pillar stem Xin, linking the year's authority directly to you and to your home and output — good for being recognised, but it can blur boundaries between work and private life. This is also a Tai Sui year, since the year branch matches your year-pillar branch, a year of more change and adjustment; keep plans flexible. The Fire season of summer is a good time to start the bigger initiatives.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The year stem Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) is a Seven Killings, favorable, keeping the theme of challenge and productive pressure. The year branch Wei 未 (Goat), however, is Earth — unfavorable — and its main qi Ji 己 (Yin Earth) is Indirect Resource, the star of indirect learning and outside support. So the year mixes a favorable push with an unfavorable tendency to absorb too much input and rely on second-hand guidance. In the first half, use the Ding momentum for something concrete; in the second half, guard against over-researching and under-acting.

Relations are unusually sociable this year: Wei forms a six harmony with your year pillar branch Wu, and three-harmony links with both your day pillar branch Hai and your hour pillar branch Mao. Harmony relations tend to smooth cooperation, so this is a good year for partnerships, joint plans and family matters — the connections are there to be used. The caution is that harmony can also mean being carried along; check that joint decisions still match what you actually want. There is no Tai Sui involvement this year.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

Both halves of this annual pillar are unfavorable: the year stem Wu 戊 (Yang Earth) is a Direct Resource, the star of conventional learning and structured support, and the year branch Shen 申 (Monkey) is Metal, with Geng 庚 (Yang Metal), a Rob Wealth, as its main hidden stem. Coming on top of a Geng Chen Luck Pillar that already carries Rob Wealth and Direct Resource, this year doubles down on the qualities your strong Day Master has plenty of. Expect a year of consolidation, study, and possibly a crowded field of peers — useful, but not naturally energising.

The one relation listed is a three-harmony link between the year branch Shen and the Chen branch of your Luck Pillar, which softens the repetition and can make this a quietly productive year for building foundations. Lean into learning, systems and anything that rewards patience, and keep your output visible so the year does not pass in preparation alone. In the second half, deliberately make room for Fire and Water activities — demanding challenges and creative expression — to counterbalance the metal and earth.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The year stem Ji 己 (Yin Earth) is an Indirect Resource, unfavorable, and the year branch You 酉 (Rooster) is Metal, also unfavorable, with Xin 辛 (Yin Metal), a Friend, as its main hidden stem. This is another resource-and-peer year: more input, more company, less natural momentum. Its signature feature is a stem combination between the year stem Ji and your month pillar stem Jia 甲 (Yang Wood) — the Direct Wealth of your career pillar. In plain terms, outside advice or support may pull at your work and income arrangements, so clarify terms rather than assuming.

The year branch also clashes with your hour pillar branch Mao, so routines, home matters and close working relationships may feel more changeable; slow down and talk things through rather than reacting. It also forms a six harmony with the Chen branch of your Luck Pillar, which offers a stabilising counterweight. Early in the year is a good time to review commitments; toward the end of the year, simplify.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The year stem Geng 庚 (Yang Metal) is a Rob Wealth, unfavorable, matching the stem of your current Luck Pillar, and the year branch Xu 戌 (Dog) is Earth, also unfavorable, with Wu 戊 (Yang Earth), a Direct Resource, as its main hidden stem. This is the most metal-and-earth-heavy year in the window, and the theme is independence and self-reliance pushed to its limit. The strength to draw on is stamina and clear standards; the habit to watch is comparison and the urge to do everything alone.

Three relations shape the year. Xu forms a three-harmony link with your year pillar branch Wu, and a six harmony with your hour pillar branch Mao — both cooperative, so partnerships and home life can actually run smoothly. But Xu also clashes with the Chen branch of your Geng Chen Luck Pillar, which can make the decade's underlying themes feel unsettled and ask you to re-check plans you thought were fixed. Keep decisions reversible in the second half, and let the harmony relations carry the social side of the year.

## Guidance

- **Build Fire into your week.** Fire is favorable and appears mainly as Officer stars, so take on one visible responsibility — a project with a real deadline — each season; it channels your strong metal into structure rather than restlessness.
- **Keep a Direct Wealth routine separate from your experiments.** Your month stem's Direct Wealth and your hour branch's Indirect Wealth are two different channels; keeping a steady saving habit apart from side ventures lets you use both without letting Rob Wealth blur them.
- **Protect sleep and mealtimes as non-negotiable.** Earth is your weakest element at 5.3%, and earth-like routine is what a 45.9% metal chart most needs to stay centred.
- **Say the appreciative thing out loud.** Your day branch's Hurting Officer and the pervasive Rob Wealth can make critique the default register; naming what you value in people uses your favorable Fire and softens the competitive edge.
- **Treat the Geng Chen decade as a study period, not a scoreboard.** Its Rob Wealth and Direct Resource are both unfavorable, while the coming Ji Mao Luck Pillar brings favorable Indirect Wealth — put time into depth now so the next decade has something to work with.
